questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a university that offered high level courses and had a beautiful campus.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy, there are many resources offered at Yale to help you. However, there was no meeting for international exchange students at the beginning of the spring semester.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a meeting at OISS on visa status and more, I only heard of this by chance through another student. Otherwise, there were no meetings or events for international exchange students at the beginning of the spring semester.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy. Look in facebook groups. I would definately suggest living in East Rock.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Yale operates shuttle buses that can transport you, but they are very unreliable and not that frequent. Be prepared to walk a lot.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Yale does not offer housing to exchange students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register online for courses through Yale Hub.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could reach out to people at Yale for help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to look at when the courses are held to make sure there is no overlap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took both master's and PhD level courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style is very different from UCPH. The classes are very small, around 8-15 students. Therefore, participation is expected. I also took a workshop, which was more like regular lectures with professors from different universities.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Inequality, race, and the city. Methods in Gender and Sexuality Studies. Frailties. Stratification and Inequality Workshop.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Inequality, race, and the city was a great course. Professor Anderson is an exceptional teacher and the course material is very rich. 
Frailties was also a very informative course on critical age studies. 
The Stratification and Inequality Workshop was great and gave a lot of different perspectives.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Food is expensive, there are no regular grocery stores in downtown New Haven. I ordered groceries through DoorDash. Otherwise, you need to know someone with a car.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transportation can also be a bit difficult, sometimes it makes the most sense to take Uber or Lyft.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports games, LGBTQIA+ events, student performances of dance and music. There are a lot of events at Yale. There are no American football games during the spring semester. Also Yale has free museums.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the sports games, especially Lacrosse.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to NYC, Boston, and some of the smaller towns in the area. Mystic has a great seaport museum.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Mostly easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Reach out and ask if people want to go for coffee.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Do not know.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Open and welcoming people at Yale.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for a lot of preparation work when applying for exchange. However, when you are abroad, there is almost no more paperwork etc.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
New Haven is very cold in the winter. It was -15 degees at one point. Bring warm clothes and shoes.
Yale has a two week spring break, use it for travel and fun times.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living with a great roommate and taking courses that were challenging and interesting.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The amount of readings for the courses could be very overwhelming.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Make sure you meet handsome Dan. There is also a taxidermied version of him at the Peabody Museum.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
